contract: Import an explicitly supplied, owned Signal Desktop SQLCipher-4 database using its transient 64-hex database key. Authenticate every page before in-memory AES-256-CBC decryption, validate the supported Signal schema, preserve conversation-scoped message provenance and attachment references, and ingest unambiguous existing-person observations into the canonical communications database. Never inspect an operator desktop, persist the key or persist decrypted database bytes.
acceptance: A database produced by the actual SQLCipher 4 CLI decrypts, validates and yields the expected Signal message and attachment metadata
Wrong keys, tampered pages, plaintext SQLite, malformed keys, unsupported sizes and unsupported schemas fail without imports
Transient key and decrypted database bytes are absent from durable state and the plaintext buffer is overwritten after every attempt
Conversation-scoped provenance, exact review binding, idempotent retry and ambiguous-person non-linking are independently asserted
Real HTTP and console upload, preview, commit, history and authentication-error journeys use the production handler
limits: The supported format is Signal Desktop's SQLCipher-4 layout with 4096-byte pages, 80 reserved bytes, AES-256-CBC and HMAC-SHA512.
The importer accepts the current Signal raw 64-hex database key; Electron safeStorage or operating-system keychain extraction is deliberately outside this owned-archive boundary.
At most 32 MiB and 1000 normalized messages are accepted per import; imported archive coverage is not a claim of complete Signal history.
Attachment metadata is preserved as a reference only; the importer never follows Signal Desktop attachment paths.

qualification.live_operator_desktop: not accessed; explicitly supplied owned encrypted archive only
